items.title: Japanese Yen futures jump ahead of national CPI report.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the recent price action in Japanese Yen futures, highlighting a recovery after six lower closes in the last seven sessions. The yen found support from the U.S. Treasury's announcement to double the size of its long-dated buybacks, increasing operations in the 10- to 30-year part of the curve to at least 4 billion. Looking ahead, Iaccino previews Japan's upcoming national CPI report, noting that June core inflation remained below the Bank of Japan's 2% target and exploring how tomorrow's numbers could influence future central bank policy and currency direction.

items.title: Treasury doubles bond buybacks.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners breaks down the morning market action, noting an early lift in stocks led by Russell 2000 futures. The spotlight shifts to the U.S. Treasury, which announced it will double the size of its long bond buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation. Bob explains how this impacts long-end yields and supports risk assets. Traders also look ahead to today's FOMC minutes release at 2:00 PM EDT for a clearer view of the recent committee rate split. Finally, he outlines the heavy schedule ahead, highlighting key corporate earnings, the PBOC rate decision, and upcoming U.S. economic data including jobless claims and the Philly Fed manufacturing index.

items.title: Calm crude, tightening diesel: the real oil market stress is downstream
items.excerpt: Key Points: Hormuz remains severely impaired : US-Iran negotiations remain deadlocked and tanker traffic through the Strait has slowed again, leaving Middle Eastern exports well below normal despite numerous efforts to reroute supply. Crude prices understate the disruption : Alternative pipelines, strategic stock releases, weak Chinese demand and demand destruction have prevented a much larger crude rally, with Brent holding around USD 90 despite the prolonged disruption. Diesel reveals the real stress: Disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian refined-product supply have pushed the WTI-ULSD and Brent-gasoil cracks to record levels around USD 103 and USD 77 per barrel respectively. Borrowing oil from the future has limits : Strategic reserves have helped bridge the supply gap, but…

items.title: Markets React to Geopolitical Tensions and Fed Outlook.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners recaps the morning's market action as U.S. equities open lower, led by a drop in Nasdaq futures. He covers rising diesel prices tied to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and breaks down the latest global economic data, including UK jobs and Eurozone sentiment. Domestically, U.S. housing starts are in focus alongside declining precious metals and climbing U.S. Treasury yields. Iaccino also examines the CME FedWatch Tool's shifting probabilities for a September rate hike ahead of critical FOMC minutes, wrapping up with a look at upcoming major retail earnings from Target, Lowe's, and TJX.

items.excerpt: Key takeaways China is not disappearing as a luxury market, but consumers are becoming more selective about where they spend. Years of price increases have tested the limits of what aspirational customers are willing to pay. Falling shares improve valuations, but Herm s, LVMH, Kering and Richemont offer very different investment cases. European luxury shares have come under pressure, reflecting weaker growth, more cautious consumers and high expectations built up over previous years. Lower share prices do not automatically create opportunities, but they are making the investment question more interesting. items.title: Copper versus gold: what an old macro signal is telling us now
items.excerpt: Key Points: Copper-to-gold ratio remains historically low : Around 3.24, still signaling gold s strength, though copper has recently recovered slightly. Macro signal is less clear : Copper reflects industrial demand, but electrification, AI buildout, supply constraints, and geopolitics now play a larger role; gold is supported by central bank buying and diversification. Copper is still an industrial meta l: Higher prices can trigger substitution, efficiency gains, and demand destruction. Gold faces fewer constraints : Driven by investment and central banks, it is less exposed to demand destruction and may outperform in a risk-hedging environment. items.title: Why higher yields are changing the investment playbook
items.excerpt: Key takeaways: Capital is getting more expensive: governments, AI, defence and infrastructure are all competing for funding. Higher yields may mean something different: if fiscal risk is driving yields, the dollar may not strengthen and gold may stay supported. Portfolio leadership could shift: investors may increasingly favour cash generation, balance-sheet strength, income and diversification over leverage and long-duration bets. Capital may be becoming the market's next scarce resource For much of the post-global-financial-crisis era, investors operated under an implicit assumption: capital was abundant. Low policy rates, central-bank asset purchases and subdued inflation reduced the cost of financing across governments and corporates. That backdrop supported long-duration bonds,…

items.title: From groceries to lipstick: seven companies test the consumer
items.excerpt: Key takeaways Walmart, Target and TJX can show whether shoppers are cutting back or simply becoming more selective. Home Depot and Klarna test appetite for larger purchases when confidence and borrowing costs still matter. Carlsberg and Est e Lauder show whether small indulgences remain resilient across different markets. US retail sales fell 0.6% in July, while consumer sentiment weakened again in early August. That sounds gloomy, but economy-wide data hides an important distinction. Households rarely stop spending everywhere at once. They change what they buy, where they buy it and how they pay. items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners breaks down price action in British Pound futures as the September contract reached a three-month high before settling higher for the session.
